what_it_does: As transistors shrink, chip designers are experimenting with stacking the two types of transistors (n-type and p-type) directly on top of each other in a single vertical column — a technology called CFET (Complementary Field-Effect Transistor). This stacking saves horizontal space but makes it extremely hard to route the wires that connect the transistors, because the available wiring tracks are scarce. This paper presents a three-stage automated layout tool: first it partitions the circuit and checks that each piece is manageable; then it uses a mathematical constraint solver (SMT — Satisfiability Modulo Theories, a tool that finds solutions satisfying a set of logical rules) to place transistors while simultaneously reserving space for the key connections; finally it routes the metal wires layer by layer, using a mix of manually inspired rules for the lowest layer and an optimization algorithm (ILP — Integer Linear Programming, finding the best assignment from a finite set of choices) for the higher layers. The result is claimed to be a practical, fully automated path to legal CFET cell layouts with guaranteed wiring feasibility.
